newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends sharply higher in brisk trading.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends sharply higher in brisk trading.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer as the market became increasingly bullish, casting aside an unexpected hike in LME stocks to coast to fresh eight-month highs in heavy trading.

"Although stocks on LME rose this morning, it was a generally bullish number," analyst Fred Demler of E D and F Man International said. Technical buying, merchant shortcovering, and fund buying combined with upward momentum in other base metals to power prices higher.
LME stocks rose a modest 1,875 tonnes to 222,500 tonnes. Traders had expected a dip of at least 3,000 tonnes.

March COMEX settled 1.90 cents higher at 113.30 cents per lb, traded 113.80 to 111.20 cents. Volume was estimated at a brisk 25,000 lots compared to Thursday's official 11,965 lots. Switches were estimated at 7,944.
Traders said copper was expected to make further gains next week when the Chinese return to the market after the New Lunar Year holiday.
Tightness rolled over from the February LME dates to April will also put a floor under prices, some brokers suggested.
The LME backwardation teetered slightly but only a couple of dollars lower at $73/$77 by COMEX close compared to Thursday.
Demler also noted that the American Bureau of Metal Statistics has just sharply revised downwards it global producer stock totals, a move which should prompt a revision in price forecasts.
